identificacion.descripcion: Microchip, register and local census: what your region requires and what national law requires for cats.

curso.descripcion: The responsible ownership course that Act 7/2023 requires to own a dog, and why it cannot be taken yet.

seguro_rc_perros.titulo: Third-party liability insurance for your dog
seguro_rc_perros.descripcion: Act 7/2023 requires it for the dog's whole life, but leaves the amount to a regulation.
seguro_rc_perros.explicacion:
The law requires you to take out and keep third-party liability insurance for damage to others for the whole life of your dog. However, it leaves the minimum amount to a regulation that has not been published yet, so today there is no national amount that can be enforced.

Note: if your region or your town council already required it on their own, it can be enforced there. And if your dog is considered potentially dangerous, the €120,000 minimum set by Royal Decree 287/2002 does apply today.

curso_tenencia_perros.descripcion: Mandatory, free and valid indefinitely, but its content is pending regulation.
curso_tenencia_perros.explicacion:
Act 7/2023 requires anyone who wants to own a dog to prove they have completed a training course. The course is free and valid indefinitely.

Its content will be set by regulation, and that regulation has not been published yet, so there is still no official course you can take to comply.

microchip_esterilizacion_gatos.titulo: Microchip and neutering for your cat
microchip_esterilizacion_gatos.descripcion: Before six months of age, except cats registered as breeding animals of a registered breeder.
microchip_esterilizacion_gatos.explicacion:
Act 7/2023 requires all cats to be identified with a microchip and surgically neutered before they are six months old.

There is one exception: cats registered in the identification register as breeding animals in the name of a breeder listed in the Register of Pet Breeders. We cannot check that case with the data we ask for, so keep it in mind if it applies to you.

Unlike the insurance and the course, this obligation does not depend on any pending regulation: it can be enforced.

licencia_ppp.titulo: Local licence for a potentially dangerous dog
licencia_ppp.descripcion: Granted by your town council. It requires insurance of at least €120,000 and is renewed every five years.
licencia_ppp.explicacion:
If your dog is considered potentially dangerous, you need an administrative licence granted by the competent body of your town council.

Among its requirements: being of legal age, clean criminal record certificates, certificates of physical fitness and psychological aptitude, and third-party liability insurance with cover of no less than €120,000.

The licence is valid for five years and can be renewed for equal periods.

identificacion_animales.descripcion: Your region requires your animal to be identified, usually with a microchip.
identificacion_animales.explicacion: Identification is a regional responsibility, so the deadline and the species covered depend on where you live. See your region's quote below.

censo_municipal.titulo: Register your animal with your town council
censo_municipal.descripcion: Your region requires you to register it in your town council's animal census.
censo_municipal.explicacion: The census is kept by your town council, but the obligation to register comes from your region's law. The exact deadline is in the quote.
